passage:
In the UKG classroom, Rukmini stood up to read the picture card. "Ell-y-fant," she said.
Laughter rippled across the room. Her cheeks burned and she wanted to shrink into her shoes.
Aparna, the teacher, raised a hand. "Everyone here is still learning words, even me. Let us say it together: el-e-phant." The class repeated it.
One boy near the front was still giggling. Rukmini took a breath. "That is unkind, Rohit."
Rohit stopped and studied his desk. Rukmini said the word again, slowly, and got it right.

qa.q: How did Rukmini feel when the class laughed?
qa.a: She felt small and embarrassed: her cheeks burned and she wanted to shrink into her shoes.

qa.q: What could Rukmini do when someone keeps laughing?
qa.a: She can say calmly that it is unkind, as she did with Rohit, and keep trying the word.

qa.q: How might Aparna see the laughter in the class?
qa.a: Aparna seems to see it as part of learning together and steps in gently, saying even the teacher is still learning, so no one is singled out.

grounding: The class laughs at a child's mispronounced word; she feels small and hot, a teacher says everyone is learning, and she says that is unkind.

passage:
"Jomon, tell us what you found in the garden," said Yamini Miss.
Jomon held up his leaf. "A pillarcater!"
The class burst out laughing. "Pillarcater!" someone squealed.
Jomon's ears went pink and he pulled the leaf to his chest.
"Everyone is learning," said Yamini Miss. "I mix up long words too. Want to try again, Jomon?"
Jomon peeked at the giggling faces. The word did sound funny. A small smile crept up. "Pillarcater," he said slowly, and giggled too.
"Cat-er-pil-lar," Yamini Miss said with him.
"Caterpillar!" This time everyone laughed together, and Jomon laughed loudest.

qa.q: What did Jomon call the creature on his leaf?
What was Jomon feeling when the class burst out laughing?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and small: his ears went pink and he pulled the leaf to his chest.

qa.q: Which choice helped Jomon, and why?
qa.a: Yamini Miss saying that everyone is learning, and Jomon choosing to giggle at the funny word, turned the laughter into something shared instead of hurtful.

qa.q: How might Yamini Miss see the first burst of laughter?
qa.a: She seems to notice it could hurt Jomon, so she reminds the class that she mixes up words too and gives him a kind second try.

grounding: A child mispronounces a word and the class laughs; a teacher says everyone is learning, and he chooses to laugh gently so the class laughs together.

passage:
Note from the class teacher, Tuesday.
During morning circle Sahil read the word of the day, "vegetable", as "veg-e-table". Divyansh shouted, "A table of veg!" and half the circle laughed. Sahil went red, pressed his lips together and slid behind the child next to him.
I paused the circle and said, "Everyone is learning. I still trip on words." I asked Divyansh how the joke might feel to Sahil.
At the water tap later, Divyansh started the joke again. I heard Sahil say, "That is unkind." Divyansh stopped. I told Sahil it was brave to speak up, and I will keep an eye on the group.

qa.q: Which word did Sahil read as "veg-e-table"?
How can you tell Sahil felt hurt by the laughter?
qa.a: He went red, pressed his lips together and slid behind another child, which shows he felt small and embarrassed.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped the circle?
qa.a: The teacher paused the circle, said everyone is learning, and asked Divyansh how the joke might feel to Sahil.

qa.q: What might Divyansh have noticed when Sahil said "That is unkind"?
qa.a: Divyansh stopped straight away, so the joke may have looked less like shared fun and more like something that hurt Sahil.

grounding: A classmate mocks a child's mispronounced word; the adult says everyone is learning and the child says "that is unkind".
